source.display_title: 05/28/2026 - Alex Rueter x Andrew Musial — Lost

setter.evidence: No setter code in the title and none named. The prospect came directly from an Instagram ad: 'I found one of his ads on Instagram' and, asked how well he knew Trevor's work, answered 'not at all actually'.

prospect.name: Alexander Rueter
prospect.location: United States — rural or suburban, with a 30-50 minute commute each way
prospect.occupation: Parks and Recreation — manages seven baseball fields and grounds maintenance; walks five to ten miles on some days and sprays sports fields. Leaves home at 05:00, works 06:00 to 14:30.
prospect.training_background: Effectively untrained. Played tennis in high school and used the college gym, then stopped after graduating. Recently started shoulder presses at home with free weights to rebuild shoulder strength. Was given a home exercise programme by a physical therapist and has stopped doing it — 'Should be, but no.' Shoots a bow for archery. Avoids gyms: 'I'm a little too shy to be working out in a gym.'
prospect.medical: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, a connective-tissue disorder, described as not recently diagnosed. Reconstructive surgery on his elbow in high school. Partially dislocated his shoulder about a month before the call, and again a few weeks before it by grabbing a swinging door — 'I grabbed the door as it was swinging shut... there was some momentum with the door, but that shouldn't be an issue.' Kneecap subluxes daily when walking — 'my kneecap does this like popping feeling, it's like dislocating a joint'. Weak and stiff hip flexors that he links to lower back pain and knee pain; ends heavy work days icing his back. Self-describes his weight as 'technically obese' though his primary care physician is not concerned. Has ADD and takes medication for it. Sees a chiropractor and has seen a physical therapist.

signals: Wants a former self back and dates it: 180-190 lb, last seen 'probably in college... 15, maybe even 20 years ago'

Carries visible regret and shame — 'Embarrassed of having this gut hanging out front', 'I have to wear a 2XL just to wear a t-shirt when I'd probably, for my frame, be in a large', and 'I feel like I'm probably 10 years older, what I should be, comparative to my friends'

Fits the type imperfectly. The ground was not lost to a bad season — Ehlers-Danlos is congenital — and he has severe price resistance, so he also carries traits of the_medically_constrained without its defining absence of price resistance

Proposed label for clustering if the vocabulary is extended: a financially-excluded, medically-complex prospect — very high intent, a genuine clinical contraindication, and no capacity to pay at any tier

goals.text: Stop being in pain day to day — chosen over appearance when asked to pick one
Build core muscle and lose the belly — from a 36 inch waist to a 30
Feel comfortable taking his shirt off at the pool or the beach
Stop his joints dislocating — strengthen around the shoulder, knee and hip so ordinary movements do not injure him
Come home from work able to mow the lawn or shoot his bow instead of sitting on ice
Shoot more than two quivers of archery before his form falls apart
Train at home, because gyms make him self-conscious
Have a system and an understanding rather than more internet options — 'I lack the understanding and the system to go towards, because there's so many options'

pains.text: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome — joints dislocate under ordinary load; shoulder partially dislocated twice in recent weeks
Kneecap subluxes daily when walking, and he walks five to ten miles for work
Lower back pain severe enough that a two-day spraying job left him icing his back each evening
Weak and stiff hip flexors that he links to the back and knee pain
Severe financial distress — $40 cash on hand, credit cards being paid down, a retirement loan taken for house repairs that will take two years to repay, plus a mortgage
Exhaustion — up at 03:00, out the door by 05:00, home mid-afternoon after a 30-50 minute commute; named this himself as the real blocker over motivation
Stopped the home programme his physical therapist gave him
Self-sabotage he can articulate — the internal voice saying 'let's see how long this one lasts'
Too self-conscious to train in a gym, partly because of people filming for social media
Eating more carbohydrates than he wants because money is tight, and a strong sweet tooth
Ageing making change feel progressively harder — 'as I start to age, it seems to be getting worse and worse to try and get into a better shape'

objections.raw_quote: I was not aware it was going to be that much, in which case now I feel terrible for taking up your time. I can't do either of them.
objections.rep_response: Ran the money play properly — isolated confidence in the programme from the money, used the should-versus-how frame, offered customised terms, asked permission for an open financial conversation, then took cash on hand and credit. On hearing $40 and a credit card being paid down, he stopped selling.

objections.raw_quote: How about when I get to the financial point that I can do this? I did get Trevor's free follow along guide. And once it's paid off, I'll reach back out to y'all.
objections.rep_response: Corrected the prospect's framing that this was about the rep's income — 'it's not about me. My life won't change if you're gonna buy or if you're not gonna buy' — then asked for a timeframe, got none, and offered to send free materials and stay in touch.

objections.raw_quote: I want to say yes. / What makes you not saying that? / Myself. Knowing myself.
objections.rep_response: Ran an improvised devil-and-angel exercise, got the prospect to name the self-doubting voice ('Let's see how long this one lasts'), then asked which one he would listen to and why this time is different.

offer.payment_plan_terms: No structure was reached. Rep said only 'Most of the clients just take it upfront, but for some of them, it shouldn't be the way that they should proceed... So we don't have any set payment plans. It's all customized depending on like what's best for the client.' No figures were put forward once cash on hand came back at $40.

prospect_financials.note: Disclosed under direct questioning: '$40 cash on hand', earmarked for petrol, with groceries already scheduled and mortgage and loan payments made. Credit cards exist but are being paid down. Also repaying money borrowed from his retirement for house repairs, which he expects to take two years. No monthly surplus, card count, available credit or investments were asked.

evidence: Explicit and immediate refusal at both tiers: 'I can't do either of them'
Absolute rather than negotiable: 'the financial is where it's going to stop. Like, that is, I have no ability to change that at this point in time'
The prospect proposed the exit himself and set no date: 'once it's paid off, I'll reach back out to y'all... I don't have a specific time for it. I'm sorry.'
No payment, no deposit, no link, and no follow-up call booked — only 'we can have another conversation in some time'

Counter-evidence that this is a lost sale rather than a lost prospect: he confirmed full belief in the programme ('are you 100% confident on the program itself... Yes') and the rep committed to sending free materials and staying in touch
outcome.next_step: Rep to send free self-directed materials within a few days and stay in contact; no call scheduled and no date agreed.

notable.note: Two things a principal needs to see, pulling in opposite directions. The clinical exposure is the most serious in this batch: a man with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, a reconstructed elbow, two partial shoulder dislocations in the preceding weeks and a kneecap that subluxes daily was taken through the full pitch and a commitment close for loaded ballistic kettlebell training. The rep knew he had a chiropractor and a physical therapist, asked whether they had prescribed exercises and whether he was doing them — and then used the fact that he had stopped as the sales argument for accountability, without ever asking whether any clinician had cleared this kind of training. Against that, the money handling was the best in the batch and should be held up as the standard: the rep ran the objection play properly, asked permission before the financial questions, and when the answer came back as $40 cash and a credit card being paid down, he stopped selling, declined to reach for financing, corrected the prospect's assumption that this was about the rep's commission, and offered free materials instead. Compare the Jorge Fernández call two days earlier, where an identical zero-cash disclosure was met with an offer of a third-party financing partner.

quality.notes: The opening four minutes and the closing three minutes are merged into single unpunctuated blocks spanning both speakers, and labels invert throughout the middle — the prospect's own line 'Which direction feels better for you?' at 00:47:26 is the rep's, and the rep's summary of the prospect's weight history at 00:16:52 runs under the prospect's label. Roles read from content. The rep never asked whether the prospect has a family, so family status is unknown.
